(Insurer of Car bearing reg.No. Ka-40-A-9275) Policy # 1003/31/21/047906 valid from 14.05.2020 to 13.05.2021 (By Sri.Gururaj Salur-Adv. Sri.K.M.Ravi - Adv.) 2. Vinay.N, Major, S/o. texts.facts: This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident. (SCCH-9) 3 MVC.No.3625/2021 2 . The brief case of the petitioner is as under: On 13.08.2020 at about 5.30 pm., the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider on the TVS Heavy Duty Moped bearing reg.No.KA-50-K-3655 along with his grand mother Smt.Gangamma and the said moped was riding by his father Ramanjinappa on the left side of Gudibande- Gowribidanur road, near Lakkasandra gate, Gowribidanur road, near Lakkasandra gate, driver of the car bearing No.KA-40-A-9275 came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner without following traffic rules and regulations, all of a sudden came from back side and dashed against the petitioner's moped from behind. Due to impact petitioner, his grand mother and his father were thrown out from the moped and sustained severe head and bodily injuries. Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Govt., General Hospital, Gowribidanur wherein first aid was done, then he was shifted to Someshwara hospital, (SCCH-9) 4 MVC.No.3625/2021 Gowribidanur wherein the petitioner was treated as inpatient and underwent wound debridement. The petitioner was 4 years at the time of accident. The Gowribidanur rural police have registered a criminal case against the driver of the car bearing No.KA-40-A- 9275 in crime No.0207/2020 under Section 279,337 and 304A of IPC. The respondent No.2 being the RC owner and respondent No.1 being the insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. 3. After service of summons, the respondent No.2 has not appeared before the court hence, placed exparte and respondent No.1 has appeared before the tribunal and filed its written statement. Lokesh Alias Lokesh Babu vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 19 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51341245/ 2 4. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.1 is that, the claim petition is not maintainable in law or on facts. It has admitted the issuance of the policy in favour of the respondent No.2. Respondent No.1 has denied the involvement of the car (SCCH-9) 5 MVC.No.3625/2021 bearing reg.No.KA-40-A-9275 in the alleged accident. It has denied the age, occupation, income and amount spent by the petitioner. Further deposed that, the owner of the vehicle did not report and furnished the RTO documents pertaining to the offending vehicle regarding the driving licence of the person who was driving the vehicle at the time of accident which required under Section 134(C) and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.158(6) of MV Act. It has contented that, at the time of accident, petitioner was not wearing safety headgear which is clear violation of MV Act. There are three persons are traveling on the motor cycle against to its seating capacity and lost control over the same and caused the accident. The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exorbitant and exaggerated. With these grounds the respondent No.1 sought for rejecting the claim petition. 5. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal (SCCH-9) 6 MVC.No.3625/2021 has framed the following issues: 6. In order to prove his case, the father of the petitioner himself examined as PW.1 and in all got marked documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P.9. Issue No.1:- It is the case of the PW-1 that, on 13.08.2020 at about 5.30 pm., he was riding the TVS Heavy Duty Moped bearing reg.No.KA-50-K-3655 along with his mother Smt.Gangamma and petitioner as his pillion riders on the left side of Gudibande-Gowribidanur road, near Lakkasandra gate, Gowribidanur road, near Lakkasandra gate, driver of the car bearing No.KA-40-A- 9275 came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner without following traffic rules and regulations, all of a sudden came from back side and dashed against the petitioner's moped from behind. Due to impact petitioner thrown out from the moped and sustained severe head and bodily injuries. 10. In order to prove the case, the petitioner himself examined as PW1 and filed affidavit in lieu of (SCCH-9) 8 MVC.No.3625/2021 chief-examination and reiterated all the facts mentioned in the petition. He also got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P.9 which are FIR, statement, mahazar, wound certificate, IMV report, charge sheet, discharge summary, adhar card, medical bills statements. 11. On perusal of police documents which are marked at Ex-P1 to Ex-P6 it is clear that the accident took place on 13-08-2020 at about 5.30 p.m., and - FIR in crime No.0207/2020 came to be registered on 13-08- 2020 i.e., on the same of accident at Gowribidanur Police Station for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337, 304A of IPC. Ex.P.2 - complaint lodged by PW-1 on 13-08-2020. Ex.P.3 is the panchanama, Ex.P4 is the wound certificate, Ex.P5 is the IMV report, Ex.P6 is the charge sheet which describe the spot of accident as towards Gowribidanur, Gudibande road, D palya cross, near Lakkasandra gate and Ex.P.7 is the discharge summary, Ex.P.5 is the IMV report which shows the damages caused the vehicles (SCCH-9) 9 MVC.No.3625/2021 which involved in the alleged accident I.e., motor cycle bearing No.KA-50-K-3655 and car bearing No.KA-40-A- 9295. Ex.P.6 is the charge sheet which has been filed against the driver of car bearing No.KA-40-A-9275. 12.
texts.arguments: The petitioner has produced ex-P9-8 medical bills for Rs.20,050/-. Further the parents of the petitioner may spent some amount towards food, nourishment, conveyance purpose. At this juncture, this tribunal relied upon the decision reported in - MFA No.3459/2021(MV-1) ( Sri. Sadath Ali Khan Va. Sri. Noor Ahmed Sayeed and another) wherein it is held that - " 26. Courts have consistently (SCCH-9) 14 MVC.No.3625/2021 held that the compensation awarded should not be diluted solely because the injured party was not wearing protective headgear. The principle of "just compensation" requires that while contributory negligence can be a factor in determining the amount of compensation, it should not result in an unjust reduction. Lokesh Alias Lokesh Babu vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 19 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51341245/ 5 NC: 2024:KHC:28807-DB had come to the conclusion that the claimant cannot take shelter under the cited case laws as there is a violation of Section 129 of the Act in not wearing the helmet at the relevant time.
